preconditions.description: Attacker must be the admin of the TransparentUpgradeableProxy contract

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the admin of the TransparentUpgradeableProxy, call upgradeTo() or upgradeToAndCall() with a malicious implementation contract address. The malicious contract can then execute arbitrary code through delegatecall, potentially stealing funds or manipulating contract state. The attack requires admin privileges which may have been obtained through social engineering, compromised keys, or improper access control in the admin management system.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The TransparentUpgradeableProxy contract allows the admin to upgrade the implementation contract. If an attacker gains admin privileges (through key compromise, social engineering, or improper access control), they can upgrade the implementation to a malicious contract that can execute arbitrary code via delegatecall, potentially stealing funds or manipulating state. The oracle checks that _getImplementation() equals an attacker-controlled address, confirming the upgrade succeeded.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Overwrite the admin storage slot to make myself (address(this)) the admin. 2. Deploy a simple malicious implementation contract. 3. Call upgradeTo() to change the proxy's implementation to my malicious contract. 4. Verify the implementation changed successfully.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.store() to overwrite the _ADMIN_SLOT with address(this). 2. Deploy a minimal malicious implementation contract. 3. Call upgradeTo() on the proxy with the malicious implementation address. 4. Call _getImplementation() through a helper interface to verify the change.
